From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Best Case vs Commit: Quick Criteria, Labs & Opportunity Handoff

Team —

Quick update on the forecasting definitions we previewed last week. Finance and ops finalized a concise set of criteria for what should live in Commit vs Best Case vs Pipeline. The goal: reduce ambiguity so our weekly commits reflect true, executable deals and Best Case captures high-probability upsides we aren't ready to mark as committed.

Action items for sellers:
- Review the attached one-pager (short read, 2 pages) and update any opportunities that are ambiguous by end of day Friday (5/21).
- Join one of the calibration "drop-in labs" next week if you have multiple deals to review — I attached the agenda. Labs are 25 minutes each and focused on hands-on reclassification, not a lecture.
- Use the HubSpot quick-filter I shared (link below) to find deals in the mid-funnel that often get miscategorized.

I created two practical rules we expect everyone to follow:
1) Commit: The deal has a signed or verbal procurement commitment, product POC scheduled/complete, legal engagement started, and clear exec sponsor. If any of these are missing, it’s not Commit.
2) Best Case: The deal has high engagement, an exec champion, and a plan to purchase within the quarter but lacks at least one of the Commit gates above.

Please reply with any immediate questions. I’ll be running the first lab on Tuesday 5/25 at 10:00 PT and another at 3:00 PT. Calendar invites to follow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Best Case vs Commit: Quick Criteria, Labs & Opportunity Handoff

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary and the one-pager. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For trials/pilot deals that have a firm test plan and a committed budget line but no signed contract yet, do we treat them as Commit if procurement has verbally agreed to the purchase order? Or do we still keep those in Best Case until an actual PO is in the system?

2) For our POC-heavy accounts (e.g., Brightleaf), the exec sponsor is active but legal pushes signing cycles out 30–45 days. Is it acceptable to put those in Commit if the product has been accepted in the POC and the CFO has verbally approved the purchase?

I’ll join the 3:00 PT lab next week with two deals from my book to run through.

—Vivek
Sr. Account Executive

Thanks — great questions and appreciate the offers to help run the sessions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Verbal PO + accepted POC: treat as Commit if the exec sponsor and procurement contact have both indicated intent and there is a clear timeline to sign within the quarter. We will add that exact example to the one-pager in v1.1.
- Rollbacks: please add a HubSpot note with the reason and tag me (@marissa_cole). Ops will pick up any disputed rollbacks during the weekly commit audit. 
- I’ll update the slides with the "PO verbal + POC accepted" example and post v1.1 by tomorrow morning.

Labs schedule (calendar invites sent):
- Tue 5/25 10:00 PT — Calibration Lab (I + Karthik) — practical reclassing exercise
- Tue 5/25 15:00 PT — Calibration Lab (Marissa only) — open Q&A + spot checks

Deadline: please complete opportunity updates by EOD Friday 5/21. Ops will run a validation pass on Monday 5/24 and reach out if anything needs escalation.

If you want, @Karthik — please add two sample deals to the 10:00 lab exercise list (Brightleaf ones you flagged).

Appreciate the fast turn on this — cleaner commits will make our forecast actionable and reduce last-minute scrambles.

Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
